title: API breakage case
description: One real API change that broke real code, recorded so a second person can re-derive every claim from the cited sources.

api_host.description: The hostname a repository's code would call. This is the join key against a manifest.

replacement.description: What callers were supposed to move to, if the provider said.

announced_at.description: ISO date of the EARLIEST public statement anywhere. null means nothing was found — which is the most interesting value in the dataset.

effective_at.description: ISO date it actually started failing. Lead time is measured from here.

signals.description: What each signal would have seen. Absent means not investigated; present-but-false means investigated and found nothing.

evidence_of_pain.description: Developers reporting the breakage. Without this, the case may be a change nobody depended on.

confidence.description: verified: every date backed by a fetched source. partial: some dates unverified. unverified: do not score this case.

available.description: Would this signal have existed to watch at the time?

detected_at.description: ISO date this signal first made the change knowable. Lead time = effective_at - detected_at.

note.description: Especially: why a signal that existed still would not have caught it.
